item.title: Shakira Teams With FIFA To Earmark $500,000 to Support Earthquake Relief in Venezuela
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we bring you the latest updates on trending news. Today, we're shining a light on a incredible charitable effort by Shakira and FIFA to support the children of Venezuela affected by the recent devastating earthquakes. Let's dive in."
[Short music transition]
Host: "On June 24, two massive earthquakes hit Venezuela, claiming over 3,300 lives, leaving 16,000 injured, and thousands more homeless. In response, Shakira has teamed up with FIFA to provide crucial support to the affected children. Through the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, they're earmarking $500,000 to help continue educating the nation's youth during the recovery process."
[Short clip of Shakira's voice from the Instagram video]
Shakira: "Today, millions of children are growing up without the education and opportunities they deserve. That's why I'm so proud to support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund."
Host: "Shakira announced that she'll be donating 100% of the profits from her 2026 FIFA World Cup anthem 'Dai Dai' to the fund. She'll also be performing at the World Cup final alongside Madonna and BTS. But that's not all - she's calling on world leaders, including the Prime Ministers of Portugal, Germany, and France, to join the cause and support the fund, which aims to raise $100 million for education efforts worldwide."
[Short music transition]
Host: "The FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund will invite trusted local organizations in Venezuela to apply for funding to help children get back into the classroom, support teachers, and restore access to learning. As Shakira said, 'If you believe every child deserves the chance to dream, please join us.' You can find more information on how to support the fund and apply for funding on their website."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today. A big thank you to Shakira and FIFA for their incredible efforts to support the children of Venezuela. We'll be keeping an eye on this story and bringing you updates as more information becomes available. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you next time!"
